account:
Today seems quiet from what I have personally seen and heard. I read my appointments this morning, made my market walk, went home at noon, reviewed the treasury during town accounts, and kept tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage before returning for afternoon office. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. Tomorrow's book includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and afternoon council letters.

The only notable administrative difficulty was the tea address: the appointment named only a neighbour at a dockside cottage. The secretary took the appointment book from its chest this morning and later said it was safely with them. They reported asking around the cottages and warehouse without identifying the host. Nevertheless, I found the neighbour waiting at the cottage near (16, 102), and our visit was ordinary and friendly. The neighbour described a quiet afternoon and a visit to the bakery, reported no pressing concerns, and invited me back for our usual tea tomorrow. I have no evidence that the vague address or the secretary carrying the book had any purpose beyond arranging my appointments.

Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. The neighbour also said the baker was busy with fresh loaves for today's market. This fits normal bread production; I have seen no reason to suspect anything unusual. No correspondence had reached the secretary when I asked earlier. I have now called the secretary over to hear any incoming business; they are visible eleven blocks away holding a writable book, but I do not yet know what it contains.
